tier_reason: Upgraded B->A. The independent eBACS/SUPERCOP harness is public (supercop-20260627 crypto_aead/measure.c, running crypto_aead/aezv4/aesni, which is in the linked mirror) and measures aes256gcmv1 on the same machine. The web-impl pages give the compiler and flags for every implementation (aezv4/aesni: clang 19.1.7 -march=native -O ...), and the results page gives the CPU (Intel Core 5 210H, Raptor Cove).

corrections.claimed_speedup: ~2.7x lower cycles/byte than aes256gcmv1 (0.26 vs 0.70 median, long+long encrypt); decrypt ~2.2x (0.26 vs 0.57); range across the page's 15 sections 1.9x (0+long) to 6.9x (64+64 forgery, noisy row) (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: long+long encrypt, AES-NI implementation crypto_aead/aezv4/aesni, cycles/byte on a real CPU via the eBACS/SUPERCOP harness. 'long' is SUPERCOP's differential rate: 1/1920 of the cycle difference between a 2048-byte and a 128-byte message (here with the same length of associated data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: aezv4/aesni fastest with clang -march=native -O -fwrapv -Qunused-arguments -fPIC -fPIE -gdwarf-4 -Wall (Debian Clang 19.1.7). The other clang/gcc -O2/-O3/-Os builds are within 1%. Baseline aes256gcmv1: fastest implementation dolbeau/aesenc-int, clang -march=native -O2 -fwrapv -Qunused-arguments -fPIC -fPIE -gdwarf-4 -Wall (Debian Clang 19.1.7); dolbeau/vaesenc-int is within 4%, and SUPERCOP's OpenSSL wrapper (opensslnew, gcc -O2) is 1.46x slower.
corrections.caveats: Public-domain dedication in the Unlicense wording (Ted Krovetz, 'free and unencumbered software'), so no patent grant. The baseline is SUPERCOP's fastest AES-256-GCM (Romain Dolbeau's AES-NI intrinsics), which beats SUPERCOP's OpenSSL wrapper, so the comparison is against a strong AES-GCM. The mirror is a stale 2016 snapshot, and the numbers come from the live bench.cr.yp.to page (supercop-20260627 dataset). eBACS results tables do not label which implementation or compiler produced each row. The aesni/compiler attribution comes from the web-impl pages. AEZ v4 was superseded by v5 (CAESAR round 3), which has about the same speed on this page (0.28).

notes: The numbers match the aezv4 and aes256gcmv1 rows of the long+long encrypt table exactly (0.26/0.26/0.27 and 0.69/0.70/0.71). The record's claim that no compiler was stated was wrong: the linked web-impl pages list per-implementation compilers and flags. Metadata checks out: 104 stars, no repo license, not a fork, last commit 2016-07-16, and the aesni/encrypt.c header is Unlicense text.

tier_reason: eBACS is a well-known independent suite with a public harness and per-implementation compilers (morus1280256v1/avx2: clang 19.1.7 -O3). It does not show a consistent win, though. MORUS-1280-256 beats aes256gcmv1 only on encrypt and on messages with no or short associated data, and loses on long+long decrypt/forgery, 1536+1536 decrypt and AD-only workloads, so it stays at B and is not upgraded like its siblings.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed, workload-dependent (derived from page data): faster than aes256gcmv1 on long+0 (1.55x encrypt, 0.69 vs 1.07; 1.19x decrypt, 0.68 vs 0.81), long+long encrypt (1.06x, 0.66 vs 0.70) and 64+64 (1.11-1.18x). Slower on long+long decrypt/forgery (0.67 vs 0.57, ~0.85x), 1536+1536 decrypt (0.82 vs 0.70) and 0+long AD-only (0.65 vs 0.32-0.33, ~0.5x).
corrections.workload: eBACS/SUPERCOP harness on a real CPU, AVX2 implementation crypto_aead/morus1280256v1/avx2, cycles/byte for all 15 sections of the page. 'long' is SUPERCOP's differential rate: 1/1920 of the cycle difference between a 2048-byte and a 128-byte message (here with the same length of associated data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: morus1280256v1/avx2 fastest with clang -march=native -O3 -fwrapv -Qunused-arguments -fPIC -fPIE -gdwarf-4 -Wall (Debian Clang 19.1.7). Baseline aes256gcmv1: fastest implementation dolbeau/aesenc-int, clang -march=native -O2 -fwrapv -Qunused-arguments -fPIC -fPIE -gdwarf-4 -Wall (Debian Clang 19.1.7); dolbeau/vaesenc-int is within 4%, and SUPERCOP's OpenSSL wrapper (opensslnew, gcc -O2) is 1.46x slower.
corrections.caveats: The claimed win is marginal and one-directional on this Raptor Cove machine. MORUS is faster than SUPERCOP's fastest AES-256-GCM on encrypt and message-only workloads (up to 1.55x on long+0 encrypt). It is about 15% slower on long+long and 1536+1536 decrypt/forgery and about 2x slower when only associated data is authenticated. The record's earlier caveat that the gap 'narrows further' on other sections was wrong, because the gap reverses. No license header in the avx2 source (CAESAR-era submission, terms unclear), so reference/study use only. The baseline is Dolbeau's AES-NI AES-GCM, not OpenSSL, and the mirror is a stale 2016 snapshot.

notes: The 0.66 vs 0.70 numbers are on the page in the correct rows, but they are cherry-picked from the best direction. Decrypt and AD-heavy sections show MORUS slower than AES-256-GCM. reject:not-faster is arguable, but it keeps a real (up to 1.55x) win on message-only encrypt. Metadata is correct: no license in morus1280256v1avx2.c, last commit 2016-07-16, 104 stars.

The headline 4.7x is the best-case encrypt direction, and decrypt/forgery is about 2x because SUPERCOP's AES-256-GCM decrypts faster than it encrypts on this machine. notes: The numbers match the tiaoxinv2 (0.15/0.15/0.16) and aes256gcmv1 (0.69/0.70/0.71) rows of the long+long encrypt table exactly. I added the decrypt figure because it halves the headline.
